head: claude/error-feed-duty-pass-wiring
title: ops: feed the trader's error feed to the duty pass, grouped for triage
body:
## What

Wires the trader's **error feed** into the `duty` pass, so a manager session can
decide what to resolve now vs. backlog.

> **Operator ask, 2026-09-02:** *"can the error feed that's in the trader bot be
> fed directly to the manager session, so you can decide what should be resolved
> immediately vs. backlogged?"*

**Every piece already existed and nothing joined them up.**
`runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl` is the durable ring behind the
`/api/bot/notifications` banner — the only surface from which a page RATE is
recoverable — and nothing read it on a cadence. `/api/bot/logs?level=error` is
the `outcomes.jsonl` feed. `.claude/skills/duty/SKILL.md` is a pass whose entire
job is *"give every detected signal an OWNER"* with a written disposition. So
this **does not invent triage** — it renders both feeds into `docs/claude/DUE.md`,
which `duty` already reads, and the existing pass does the deciding.

## The measured cost of the gap

`ict_scalp_avax_5m` on `bybit_1` signalled 8 times in one day and placed **zero**
orders — every one rejected by the venue for an oversized qty
(`order_qty:2299510000000 > max_qty:2200000000000`). Third recurrence across
three backlog rows, and it surfaced only because the operator pasted the feed by
hand.

Against the **live feeds** it now renders as `ERRFEED-88878657`, **rank 5 of 70**:

```
- **[error] x17** `bot_logs` — api_call bybit_place_order_failed: ... too large,
  order_qty:N > max_qty:N (ErrCode: N)
  - 2026-08-23T21:42:55 -> 2026-09-02T09:06:11 · symbols=AVAXUSDT
```

## Design notes worth reviewing

- **Three read states, never collapsed** — `read` / `unreachable` / `absent`. A
  feed nobody could reach must never render as a quiet one; that is the
  `curl ... || echo '{}'` class CLAUDE.md names.
- **State the population.** `operator_alerts` is *not* a fixed window (300-600
  rows), so each feed carries its own measured `oldest_ts`/`newest_ts` and a
  `truncated` stamp. No rate is computed over an assumed window.
- **Grouping is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** Measured over the live 1000-row
  page: **866 rows were six MGC/MES no-candle causes**. A row dump would
  reproduce the flood it exists to summarise.
- **Ordering is on the level the PRODUCER stamped**, errors before warnings —
  a fact, not a severity this script assigns. It is what lifts a 17-row venue
  rejection above a 171-row no-candle flood.
- **The watermark lives INSIDE the committed digest.** `runtime_logs/` is
  gitignored and VM-local, so a re-provision would replay the whole feed. It
  advances *only* on a feed actually read — advancing on a failed fetch would
  mark an unread window as covered, the one way this design can lose a signal
  permanently.
- **The due-list render is CAPPED at 10 error groups** with an
  `ERROR-FEED-SUMMARY` row stating what was left out, so a capped render can
  never read as the whole feed.

## Three defects found in this script's own output and fixed before landing

Verified against the live feed, not just the self-test:

1. A long **decimal** was eaten as a hex blob — the AVAX cause key read
   `order_qty:<hex> > max_qty:<hex>`, hiding that the comparison was a **size
   cap**, which is the whole finding.
2. The account facet matched a venue-prefixed **shape**, so it filed the AVAX
   rejection under an account called `bybit_place_order_failed` and the IB pages
   under `ib_target_naked`. A false facet reads as attribution and sends triage
   somewhere that does not exist. Accounts are now **projected over
   `config/accounts.yaml`**, and an unreadable roster reports `accounts_state`
   rather than an empty list.
3. The **JSON-body symbol form** was missed, so the one group that most needed
   attributing carried no symbol.

Each has a named regression control.

## Cadence honesty

The cron is hourly and **declared best-effort**. `probes.yml` has exactly one
scheduled run ever (#34, ~4h50m late against `20 5 * * *`), so nothing here
claims an hourly feed: the digest carries its own `generated_at`/`covers_since`,
and `src_error_feed` raises a **loud** `ERROR-FEED-DIGEST-STALE` past 6h. A busy
feed never fails the run (that would be the desensitized-alarm P1); only a broken
runner does.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `error_feed_digest.py --self-test` | PASS — 8 property groups, 13 controls |
| `tests/test_error_feed_digest.py` | **20 passed, 0 failed** — see caveat |
| Live run against both feeds | `verdict=all_feeds_read`, 70 groups / 1365 rows |
| AVAX leg in `DUE.md` | present as `ERRFEED-88878657` |
| `run_guards.py --base main` | **69 PASS / 3 FAIL** |
| `diagnostic-provenance --all` | OK |
| `workflow-catalog` / `cron-failure-watch` | OK (both failed first — registered) |

⚠️ **Honest caveats:**

- **`pytest` is not installed in this sandbox.** The 20/20 above was obtained by
  executing every test body through a minimal `pytest.raises`/`tmp_path` shim,
  not by a real pytest run. Treat CI's run as the authority.
- The 3 failing guards are `artifact-validity-guard`, `operator-owed-guard`
  (both `No module named pytest`) and `layer-guard` (`lint-imports` exit **127**,
  command not found) — sandbox tooling, not this diff.
- Writing the test file surfaced a genuine loader bug: `@dataclass` needs the
  module in `sys.modules`, so the spec-only import raised at collection. Fixed;
  real pytest would have hit it too.

## Tier

**Tier-1** — read-only against the bot. No bot-side change, no order path, no
config, no VM mutation. The diag bearer serves `GET /api/diag/*` only;
`/api/bot/logs` is unauthenticated by design.
